- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot true values, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: overestimates after high peaks, then underestimates as prices correct downward.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true values often dip below forecast mid-to-late period, suggesting model fails to capture short-term volatility decay.
- Model underestimates prices in low-range history periods (e.g., 60–70 range) and overestimates in high-range (e.g., 75–85), indicating calibration drift.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture sudden downward corrections or “sudden drops” in true outcomes.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias: true values often dip below forecast only after 15–20 days, suggesting model doesn’t adjust for momentum decay.
- Forecast error is asymmetric: overestimates more in upward trends, underestimates in downward trends — model lacks directional sensitivity.
